author: sjm41
body:
* **PTHR ID & PTN node:**
PTN000038987 (PTHR10344)

* **Sequences with problematic annotation (ID + gene/protein name):**
Dmel Dtymk (FBgn0034299)
human DTYMK (P23919)
etc

* **Type of Issue: Erroneous source or erroneous propagation**
Both?


This node [THYMIDYLATE KINASE (PTHR10344)](http://www.pantherdb.org/panther/family.do?clsAccession=PTHR10344), includes Dmel Dtymk human DTYMK which are **deoxy**nucleoside monophosphate kinases, primarily [dTMP kinase activity] (https://www.ebi.ac.uk/QuickGO/term/GO:0004798)

However, the current annotation on this node is:
nucleoside diphosphate kinase activity (ie. non-deoxy, acting on nucleoside **di**phosphate
based on:
(YEAST\|SGD=S000003818\|UniProtKB=P00572).


That source annotation is valid, but the same source paper shows that [dTMP kinase activity] is the major activity.

So I think the MF on this node should be [dTMP kinase activity], which would match the node's name.

That said, I noticed that this node contains 2 human proteins - the other is "UMP-CMP kinase 2, mitochondrial" ([Q5EBM0](http://www.uniprot.org/uniprot/Q5EBM0)), so it looks like the family may need splitting, or else the annotation needs to go higher up the tree to something like "[GO:0019205 nucleobase-containing compound kinase activity](https://amigo.geneontology.org/amigo/term/GO:0019205#display-lineage-tab)"
title: PTN000038987 (PTHR10344)

author: marcfeuermann
body: It seems that the annotation has been partially corrected since the whole family was annotated to "dTMP kinase activity" . I completed the updates according to your suggestions. I do not think it would be easy to split the tree to remove the node containing "UMP-CMP kinase 2, mitochondrial" (Q5EBM0) since both nodes are linked to the same "ancestral" bacterial genes and are evolutionary related. Q5EBM0 is able to phosphorylate dUMP, dCMP, CMP, UMP and monophosphates of the pyrimidine nucleoside analogs. I choose the solution to use less granular parent terms for the annotation of this node.
